acceptanceCriteria.description: [happy] Given this repository at this slice's reviewed head or any later head, when node bin/rcf.js define readiness --check skeleton, --check shapes, --check stories, --check crosscut and --check consistency run, then each exits 0 and reports each of its checks [ok], including skeleton:reqShape, skeleton:tadPersistence, skeleton:deployAdr, shapes:tacHasInterface, shapes:draftSettled, shapes:templateMarkers, stories:usFloors, stories:closedSets, crosscut:securityArchitecture, crosscut:catalogue, consistency:contradictions, consistency:unsatisfiable and consistency:orphanInterfaces.

[failure] Given rcf/manifest.json at this slice's reviewed head or any later head, when every defineD4:failure and defineD4:mustNot opt-out is read, then each names its REQ and carries a non-empty reason; and every concern-ledger entry with disposition waived carries a non-empty reason (node bin/rcf.js define ledger concerns list --json shows none without one). An opt-out or waiver with an empty reason fails this criterion.

[must-not] No criterion text in this repository changes meaning to clear a readiness finding: a criterion whose wording a check flags (closedSets, unsatisfiable, contradictions) is retired and succeeded with the rcf-schemas supersession fields, or the record the check asks for (a closed set owner, a recordShape field) is added; git diff 639f07bb..<this slice's reviewed head or any later head> shows no description, given, when or then rewritten in place on a live criterion.

[non-functional] Given this repository's chain at this slice's reviewed head or any later head (about 1300 documents or more, the typical case), node bin/rcf.js define readiness --check all finishes within 2 seconds on the host the suite runs on (the test prints os.cpus().length and process.version) (it reported 29 ms compute at 639f07bb).
